transfer_provisions.section: Chapter XXI, XXI-1 to XXI-4 (prescribed by the order)
transfer_provisions.quote: Officers of the Foreign Service shall familiarize themselves with those provisions of the laws of the United States which relate to the acquisition and loss of American nationality and shall perform such duties in connection therewith as may be provided for by law or by administrative regulations prescribed by the Secretary of State.
transfer_provisions.note: Successor chapter on nationality, passports, registration and protection, prescribed in the same order that cancels Part I Chapters X, XI, XII and Part II Chapter X and revokes nine Executive Orders.

cancellations_read: 'The following-named provisions of the Foreign Service Regulations of the United States are hereby canceled: Part I: Chapters X, XI, and XII; Part II: Chapter X'.
effective_date_reading: The revocation paragraph has no effective-date, delayed-effect or phase-in wording. The held text layer separates the heading ('The following-described Executive orders are hereby revoked:') from the list by the front-page contents column and the second page's masthead (a two-page FR layout artifact); the list then runs straight into the signature block ('Franklin D Roosevelt, The White House, July 11, 1941. [No. 8820]'), so it belongs to this order. EO 8820 was signed July 11, 1941, filed July 12 and printed 6 FR 3421-3422 on July 15, 1941. The project takes an order with no effective wording to be effective on signing, so the revocations are dated 1941-07-11. The page check of the PDF is still advisable because the list is out of column order in the text layer.

targets_in_batch_07.EO:5621: revocation list, 'Executive Order No. 5621, dated May 13, 1931'; whole order, no qualifier
targets_in_batch_07.EO:5973: revocation list, 'Executive Order No. 5973, dated December 15, 1932'; whole order, no qualifier

conclusion: EO 8820 (signed 1941-07-11, 6 FR 3421-3422, read once in full from the held FR text) prescribes Chapter XXI of the Foreign Service Regulations (nationality, passports, registration, protection), cancels Part I Chapters X, XI and XII and Part II Chapter X, and revokes nine Executive Orders by number and date (No. 4359-A, 4488, 4605-A, 4893, 5032, 5549, 5621, 5773 and 5973) with no qualifier, exception, savings or pending-matter wording. EO 5621 and EO 5973 are in the list. Both amended Consular Regulations text on nationality and passports, and Chapter X of Part II is the chapter this order cancels. Whether either order's clauses ended earlier than 1941-07-11 (the Nationality Act of 1940, effective 1941-01-13; EO 8036 of 1939-01-18, which cancelled Part II section X-167) is a separate earlier-end question that this reading does not decide; both targets are blocked on it in this batch.
